verdicts.rationale: The answer omits the running guard: Health only changes Status to reset-required and sets LastError inside if c.running, so a stopped poisoned component reports stopped with empty LastError. Its stated poison/error behavior is therefore not fully correct for the source.

handleQueryMembersNATS places the poison check before context creation, unmarshalling and community lookup; graphStateContractError supplies the loaded-poison condition and exact fatal wrapper. Neither body alone establishes both ordering and the returned fatal error.

GetIncomingRelationships builds one validated RelationshipInfo per accepted composite key without deduplication, whereas getIncomingNeighbors validates the predicate and deduplicates source IDs. Both different-file bodies are required for this comparison.

The two bodies show fields, branching on noteGateOutcome and dropping unknown deferReasons, but they omit the first/change-versus-repeat policy, metric name and graph.AllDeferReasons binding. Those answer facts are defined in other entities or comments outside the catalogue body boundaries.

ApplyDefaults alone establishes the zero-to-3 assignment, but the answer also asserts DefaultConfig uses 3 and the README table/example use 2. Those facts are outside its single gold body, so this precise set does not establish the whole answer despite the real README lookalike.

FindSimilar itself establishes fail-open, the nil-client case, returned helper errors and the SemanticGapDetector consumer through an in-body comment. The additional answer claim about the clustering consumer using error-preserving findSimilarClassified appears outside this gold body, so the single entity is insufficient.
